correctness.rationale: For the seven-vertex regular cyclic tournament arcs i->i+d (d=1,2,3), independently exhaustively enumerated 2^21 arc subsets, tested in/out-degree≤1 and no directed cycles; exactly 2927 faces including empty, nonempty f-vector (21,168,630,1113,819,175). Nonidentity C7 translation cannot stabilize any nonempty face because every arc orbit size seven and a path forest has≤6 arcs. Independently constructed signed quotient cellular boundaries on orbit representatives, confirmed ∂²=0 and all integer Smith factors by degree: d1 1^2; d2 1^21 and 7; d3 1^68; d4 1^88 and 7^2; d5 1^20. Thus quotient H0=Z,H1=Z/7,H3=Z⊕(Z/7)^2,H4=Z^7,H5=Z^5. Independently enumerated complete acyclic reduced Morse matching upstairs (1416 pairs, critical 24/54/17 in d3/4/5), verified d4 has eleven unit Smith factors and d5 zero, giving torsionfree reduced ranks 13/43/17. Transfer over Q yields rational C7 modules H3=1⊕W²,H4=1^7⊕W^6,H5=1^5⊕W² where W=Q(zeta7). All matrices computed from underlying arcs independently, not saved verifier stdout.

evidence: Multipath simplices are sets of arcs forming disjoint directed paths, equivalently matching-like directed configurations with in/out degree≤1 and no directed cycles; path homology for a digraph is a different chain construction.

originality.rationale: Caputi–Collari–Di Trani–Smith original multipath-complex theorem computes transitive tournaments; this cyclic strongly connected tournament is nontransitive. General quiver-minor results require acyclicity for their comparison with matching complexes and do not determine this exact quotient torsion. Resultary closest cyclic-tournament path homology refers to different directed path homology rather than the multipath simplicial complex. No inspected prior supplies this integral seven-primary quotient table.
residual_risks: This is an exhaustive result only for this particular regular seven-vertex tournament; no all-prime or all-order assertion.
The 2024 quiver-minor article was not fully inspected; an unindexed same-tournament quotient computation remains possible.
The precise integral Z[C7]-module and geometric torsion cycle representatives are not claimed.

value.rationale: The smallest natural regular seven-vertex cyclic tournament gives a complete integral orbit-space classification, including two independent order-seven classes in H3 despite torsion-free homology of its covering complex, and the complete rational rotation module. This is a meaningful exact invariant of a natural equivariant topological object, not a known-table recomputation.
